awd_titl_txt: RAPID: Aftershock Rapid Response to the Mw 7.7 Panama 2026 Earthquake
awd_abstract_narration:
On October 9, 2026, a magnitude 7.7 earthquake occurred in the greater Panama region. This earthquake triggering an energetic and extensive aftershock sequence. Early satellite observations show surface rupture along the Azuero–Soná fault system. The widespread aftershock activity suggests additional faults were then activated. The geometries and interactions of those faults are poorly understood. This project will deploy nodal seismometers across the region in collaboration with researchers from the University of Panama and OVSICORI-UNA in Costa Rica. They will record aftershocks for several weeks, providing high-resolution observations that would be otherwise unachievable.
 
The project will generate a unique, openly accessible seismic dataset to advance understanding of earthquake rupture processes, fault interactions, and seismic hazards in this tectonically complex region. The results will provide valuable information for seismic hazard assessments, particularly for populated communities and critical infrastructure near the Panama Canal, an essential corridor for global trade. The project will also strengthen international scientific collaboration, provide hands-on training opportunities for students and local scientists, and promote the exchange of modern seismic monitoring and data-analysis techniques. Continuous seismic waveform data and station metadata will be archived through the EarthScope Data Management Center, and derived earthquake catalogs and analysis workflows will be shared with the broader scientific community.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.
